tree_commit_note: the commit that CONTAINS the measured code, golds and ranking. An earlier revision of this file recorded the PARENT commit, which had the stopword leak, the flat ranking and the rigged prefix queries, so reproducing from it gave different numbers.

code.bar_note: MEASURED FLOOR, not the 0.30 spec bar. The pre-Phase-1 baseline commit 579568d re-runs at 0.10 on the SAME live index, so the 0.30 was index drift, not a code regression: bin/lib/*.mjs is no longer in global.db, only stale graft/*.md cards remain. A rebuild was authorized and backed up (4.48 GB, quick_check ok, 852372 cards), then stopped by a real 6.0 GB RAM guard with 5.7 GB free. Decision on record: record the floor, close nothing.

fact.bar_note: First measured-reachable bar. Reached 0.90 with queries drawn from the MIDDLE of each gold, after review showed the first version used each gold's own opening words, which is a rigged benchmark.

person.bar_note: First measured-reachable bar. Reached 1.00. The original 0.00 was structural: 0 of 10 queries named their own gold and 3 of 10 golds were absent from people.db.

regressions.default_kb_search_output: byte-identical to a golden captured before any production change
regressions.code_slice_vs_0.30_spec_bar: NOT MET; the bar is stale. See slices.code.bar_note.

review: four adversarial rounds in Phase 3, one in Phase 4; this run fixed 2 BLOCKERs and 5 MAJORs before the measurement
gold_set_note: Person and fact gold sets were rebuilt in Phase 4. As shipped in Phase 0, 0 of 10 person queries named their own gold and 0 of 10 fact golds existed anywhere in the corpus, so both 0.00s measured the gold set rather than retrieval. Every replacement gold is a real record verified present in people.db / journal.db before use; fact queries draw from the middle of the gold, not its opening, and a test asserts gold/query token overlap so a rigged set fails the build.
